title: [Feature] Export repo issues & sub-issues to json
author: yiddytlq
body:
### Summary

Create am export of all issues (including sub-issues) from the repository into a single `issues.json` file. The output should be a structured JSON representation that captures essential metadata for each issue and its sub-issues.

### Details

### Requirements
- We should collect:
  - Issue number, title, body, labels, assignees, state (open/closed), creation date, last updated date.
  - Relationships to sub-issues (nested structure if available).
- Output must be a valid JSON file (`issues.json`) located in the repository root.
- The JSON should be easy to consume programmatically (clear nesting for sub-issues, arrays for labels/assignees, etc.).

### Tools
- GitHub CLI (`gh`) and/or GitHub Copilot Agent extension may be used to query issues and format the data.
- Prefer native GitHub CLI output formats (e.g., `gh issue list --json ...`) before custom scripting.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Running the workflow produces an `issues.json` file in the repo root.
- The file contains **all issues** with metadata and sub-issue relationships intact.
- JSON validates with no syntax errors.

**Example Output (`issues.json`):**  
```json
[
  {
    "id": 123,
    "title": "Main issue",
    "state": "open",
    "author": "alice",
    "labels": [
      "feature"
    ],
    "body": "Main issue body",
    "created_at": "2025-08-20T12:34:56Z",
    "comments": [
      {
        "id": 456,
        "body": "First comment",
        "author": "alice",
        "created_at": "2025-08-22T12:34:56Z"
      }
    ],
    "sub_issues": [
      {
        "id": 790,
        "title": "Sub-issue 1",
        "state": "open",
        "author": "alice",
        "labels": [
          "feature"
        ],
        "body": "Sub-issue body",
        "created_at": "2025-08-22T12:34:56Z",
        "comments": [
          {
            "id": 500,
            "body": "First comment",
            "author": "sam",
            "created_at": "2025-08-25T12:34:56Z"
          }
        ],
        "sub_issues": [
          {
            "id": 900,
            "title": "Sub-issue 1",
            "state": "open",
            "author": "sam",
            "labels": [
              "feature"
            ],
            "body": "Sub-issue body",
            "created_at": "2025-08-25T12:34:56Z",
            "comments": [
              {
                "id": 1010,
                "body": "First comment",
                "author": "alice",
                "created_at": "2025-08-29T12:34:56Z"
              }
            ],
            "sub_issues": []
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## Expected Fields for Issues and Sub-Issues

### Top-Level Fields (for every issue/sub-issue)
1. `id` — Unique numeric identifier of the issue.
2. `title` — The title of the issue.
3. `state` — `"open"` or `"closed"`.
4. `author` — GitHub username of the issue creator.
5. `labels` — Array of label names, e.g., `["bug", "feature"]`.
6. `body` — The full text description of the issue.
7. `created_at` — ISO timestamp of when the issue was created.
8. `comments` — Array of comment objects (see below).
9. `sub_issues` — Array of nested sub-issues, each with the same structure.

### Comment Object Fields (inside `comments` array)
1. `id` — Unique numeric identifier for the comment.
2. `body` — Text of the comment.
3. `author` — GitHub username of the commenter.
4. `created_at` — ISO timestamp of when the comment was created.

### Notes
- `sub_issues` can be empty (`[]`) if the issue has no children.
- `labels` and `comments` should always be arrays, even if empty.
- This schema applies recursively to all levels of sub-issues.

### Tasks
- [ ] Fetch issues, sub-issues, and comments
- [ ] Format export into issues.json file

### Related Issues

_No response_

### Priority

Medium

### Additional Notes

Comment the exact script that gives us this output too.

title: [Bug] Identify cause of date formatting and animation issue.
author: yiddytlq
body:
### Summary

Since fixing the lint errors I noticed that the date doesn't display the same anymore

### Steps to Reproduce

Build and run the project with a valid date

### Expected Behavior

1. The seconds field (potentially other fields too) should display the amount of seconds with only 2 numbers showing.
2. The animation in all date fields should show as if the number is falling (or rising if the date is in the past) when changing.

### Actual Behavior

1. The seconds shows 3 numbers when the 1st minute is finished with the 0 staying and then 4 numbers when the next minute ends with that 0 also staying and so on... In short after each minute ends a number gets added instead of both numbers just being replaced.
2. The numbers change without any animation at all. They just change.

### Related Issues

_No response_

### Severity

Major

### Additional Notes

The issue will only show on the feature/issue-42-feature-epic-code-quality-standards-migration branch as that's where the changes have been made. Any fixes made should then be merged into the branch feature/issue-42-feature-epic-code-quality-standards-migration accordingly

title: [Feature] Epic: Project Modernization & Code Quality
author: yiddytlq
body:
### Summary

Consolidate and oversee all major modernization and code quality initiatives for the project. This epic will serve as the top-level tracking issue for updates, migrations, and standardization efforts, ensuring a consistent, maintainable, and high-quality codebase.

### Details

This master epic encompasses multiple sub-epics and feature initiatives aimed at modernizing the project and enforcing consistent development standards:
- Styling Modernization: Migrate existing CSS to Tailwind CSS for maintainable, utility-first styling (#2).
- Package Management Update: Transition from Yarn to npm to simplify dependency management and CI/CD workflows (#3).
- TypeScript Migration: Convert the codebase from JavaScript to TypeScript for stronger type safety, better developer experience, and improved maintainability (#25).
- Code Quality & Standards: Enforce consistent linting, code style, and file structure standards to reduce errors and improve readability (#42).

All sub-issues related to code quality, linting, ESLint configuration, file extensions, and other enhancements (#27–#41) fall under this structure.

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Evaluate package manager support: npm, yarn, or both
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Research and decide on the package manager strategy for this project (npm vs Yarn).  
Deliver a clear recommendation with rationale and a concrete implementation plan.

### Details

**Objective:**  
Determine the optimal package manager for the project considering performance, developer experience, tooling compatibility, and long-term maintainability.

**Tasks:**
- Evaluate `npm` and `yarn` across multiple dimensions:
  - **Performance:** Install speed, caching, and Docker build times (important for CI/CD efficiency).
  - **Stability & Ecosystem Maturity:** Frequency of updates, backward compatibility, and community adoption.
  - **Tooling Compatibility:** Integration with monorepos, workspaces, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Docker builds, and CI/CD pipelines.
  - **Security:** Lockfile integrity, audit tooling, vulnerability reporting, and dependency verification.
  - **Developer Experience:** Ease of use, CLI ergonomics, documentation quality, and community support.
- Compare results against project requirements and future plans (full TypeScript adoption, Tailwind usage, monorepo or multi-package structure).
- Provide a recommendation:
  - If supporting **only one**, outline migration steps, update documentation, CI/CD configurations, and remove the other.
  - If supporting **both**, create a compatibility matrix, verify scripts under both package managers, and document caveats.
- Optional: Consider whether `pnpm` should be included in the evaluation for future-proofing and performance benefits.

**Deliverables:**
- Comparative report (table or document) summarizing findings across all dimensions.
- Clear recommendation: use `npm`, use `yarn`, or support both.
- Implementation plan detailing steps, timelines, and CI/CD adjustments.

### Related Issues

_None_

### Priority

Medium

### Additional Notes

- Emphasize Docker build times, as fast and reliable builds are critical.
- Ensure evaluation accounts for full TypeScript and Tailwind CSS adoption.
- Include any additional considerations relevant to long-term maintainability and developer productivity.

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Convert project to TypeScript
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Migrate the existing JavaScript codebase to TypeScript to improve maintainability, catch type errors at compile-time, and enhance the developer experience with better IntelliSense and tooling support.

### Details

The migration should:  
- Introduce a `tsconfig.json` with sensible defaults for a React + Tailwind project.  
- Convert all `.js` and `.jsx` files to `.ts` or `.tsx` as appropriate.  
- Replace any implicit `any` types with proper type definitions where possible.  
- Update imports, exports, and function signatures to use TypeScript types.  
- Install and configure `@types/*` packages for all dependencies.  
- Ensure ESLint and Prettier configurations are updated for TypeScript support.  
- Update build tooling (Vite/Webpack/Parcel) and test runners (if applicable) to handle TypeScript.  
- Ensure all tests pass after migration.

title: ✨Set up Copilot instructions
author: yiddytlq
body:
# Setup Copilot Instructions

## Summary

Create a `.github/copilot-instructions.md` file for this repository to configure GitHub Copilot Coding Agent according to best practices and tailored to our development workflow.

---

## Detailed Requirements and Workflow

The Copilot Coding Agent should be configured to:

1. **Analyze and Refine Issues**
   - Automatically review new and existing GitHub issues.
   - Improve clarity, add missing details, and suggest duplicates or merges.
   - Assign refined issues back to me (`@yiddytlq`) for review and approval.

2. **Implementation Planning**
   - For approved issues, generate detailed implementation plans or alternative approaches as comments.
   - Suggest complete and well-documented code snippets or file structures as drafts in comments or in a dedicated branch.

3. **Branch & Commit Workflow**
   - After I approve an implementation plan, Copilot should create a **new feature branch** named clearly based on the issue.
   - Develop the required code changes on that branch **without committing or pushing** anything until I explicitly approve.
   - Provide diffs or previews of proposed changes for my inspection.

4. **Commit & Test**
   - Upon my approval of the proposed changes, Copilot should commit the changes locally.
   - I will perform testing and validation on the branch manually.

5. **Pull Request Creation**
   - Once I have validated the branch, I will reassign the issue back to Copilot.
   - Copilot will then create a pull request (PR) from the feature branch to the main branch.
   - The PR must include a detailed description referencing the issue, the changes made, and any relevant notes.

6. **Autonomy and Controls**
   - At no point should Copilot **commit code, push branches, or create PRs without my explicit approval**.
   - All actions requiring code changes or repository modification require manual user confirmation.
   - Maintain a clear audit trail of suggestions, comments, and requested approvals.

---

## Project Overview

**simple-countdown** is a lightweight, self-hostable countdown timer web app designed for easy deployment via a single Docker Compose file.  
It is a fork and major enhancement of the [easy-countdown](https://github.com/Yooooomi/easy-countdown) project, aiming to provide:  
- Responsive UI with customizable appearance via environment variables  
- Support for multiple countdown pages and an optional admin interface  
- Full DevOps pipeline integration with automated testing, linting, and Docker image publishing  

## Primary Goals

- Maintain simplicity and lightweight footprint suitable for single-container deployment  
- Provide extensive UI customization options controlled via environment variables  
- Ensure mobile and desktop responsiveness with Tailwind CSS v4 (no config file)  
- Support multiple countdown pages configurable via Docker environment or admin panel  
- Enable smooth developer workflow with GitHub Issues, branching, PR reviews, and CI/CD  

## Coding Standards and Practices

- Use React for the frontend, with functional components and hooks  
- Use Tailwind CSS v4 utility classes for styling exclusively  
- Write clean, maintainable, and well-commented code  
- Write automated tests where applicable (unit/integration/UI)  
- Use semantic commit messages and descriptive PR titles  
- Follow the issue and PR workflow strictly for features and bugfixes  

## Areas to Assist

- Refining and clarifying GitHub Issues and Pull Requests  
- Suggesting implementation improvements or alternative approaches  
- Generating complete, tested, and documented code snippets or files  
- Detecting and suggesting deduplication of issues or code  
- Writing automated tests and documentation updates  
- Proposing optimizations for responsiveness, accessibility, and performance  

## Exclusions

- No backend beyond what is required for static hosting and config management  
- Avoid adding heavy dependencies or complexity that increases the Docker image size significantly  

## Important Links

- Original project: https://github.com/Yooooomi/easy-countdown  
- Current repo: (https://github.com/yiddytlq/simple-countdown)  
---

Please use these instructions as the definitive context for all tasks, suggestions, and automated assistance related to this repository.

title: [Feature] Epic: UI Customization & Environment Variable Driven Features
author: yiddytlq
body:
### Summary

This epic tracks all UI customization improvements and environment variable support to make the countdown timer highly configurable and user-friendly.

### Details

Includes the following sub-tasks/issues:

- Color, font size, font family customizations for timer and title
- Text visibility improvements (overlays, shadows)
- Show/hide seconds and labels toggle
- Text alignment and container styling (border, radius)
- Countdown format customization
- Auto-reload and redirect behavior on countdown end
- Favicon customization with URL or file upload support
- Multi-page countdown support with per-page settings

All features should be driven by environment variables and optionally configurable via an admin UI.

### Related Issues

_No response_

### Priority

Medium

### Additional Notes

- Sub-issues should link to this epic. - This epic is crucial for making simple-countdown versatile and user-friendly.

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Custom Logo Support
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Allow users to customize the logo displayed in the header of the countdown app. The logo URL or image should be configurable via environment variables or admin UI.

### Details

Currently, the app uses a fixed logo or no logo at all. This feature will allow users to customize the logo either by providing an image URL via an environment variable or by uploading a file through the admin page. 

When multiple countdown pages are supported, each page should be able to have its own custom logo (file upload or URL).

The logo should be responsive and display properly across different screen sizes.

Environment variable (optional): `CUSTOM_LOGO_URL` — URL of the custom logo image to display if no file is uploaded.

### Related Issues

_No response_

### Priority

Medium

### Additional Notes

- Consider fallback to default logo if none is provided or URL is invalid.
- Ensure logo does not break mobile or desktop layouts.

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Color Customization
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Add support to customize the color of the countdown digits via environment variables and admin UI, allowing users to change the timer color to fit their design preferences.

### Details

Currently, the countdown digits have a fixed color. This feature should enable users to specify the color of the timer digits through an environment variable or via the admin page.

When multiple countdown pages are supported, each page should allow independent timer color customization.

Environment variable (optional): `TIMER_COLOR` — CSS color value for the countdown digits (e.g., "#FF0000" or "rgb(255,0,0)").

### Related Issues

_No response_

### Priority

Medium

### Additional Notes

- Ensure that the color change does not affect readability or accessibility.
- Provide sensible defaults and validation for color inputs.

Each countdown page (when multi-page support is added) should be able to set its own font family.

Environment variable (optional): `TIMER_FONT_FAMILY` — CSS font-family value (e.g., "Arial, sans-serif", "'Courier New', monospace").

Medium

sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Enable users to customize the countdown display format (e.g., `DD:HH:mm:ss`) to better fit their specific needs or preferences.

### Details

Currently, the countdown format is fixed. This feature should allow users to specify a custom format string via environment variables or admin UI.

Environment variable (optional): `COUNTDOWN_FORMAT` — string representing the desired countdown format, supporting placeholders like `DD` (days), `HH` (hours), `mm` (minutes), `ss` (seconds).

sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:

Allow users to toggle the display of labels such as `Days`, `Hours`, `Minutes`, and `Seconds` next to the countdown digits.

### Details

By default, labels are shown. This feature will let users hide or show these labels using an environment variable or admin UI.

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Auto Reload Page When Countdown Ends
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Implement functionality to automatically reload the countdown page once the timer reaches zero.

### Details

Currently, the timer continues counting upwards silently after reaching zero. This feature will reload the page automatically to reflect updated content or reset the timer.

Environment variable (optional): `AUTO_RELOAD` — boolean (`true`/`false`) to enable or disable this behavior.

### Related Issues

_No response_

Medium

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Redirect URL After Countdown Finishes
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Allow users to specify a URL to which the page will redirect automatically when the countdown reaches zero.

### Details

Instead of just reloading or continuing, the countdown page should optionally redirect to a specified URL after the timer ends.

Environment variable (optional): `REDIRECT_URL` — full URL string for redirect target.

This feature should override auto-reload if both are set.

### Related Issues

_No response_

Medium

### Additional Notes

- Provide fallback behavior if the URL is invalid or unreachable.

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Improve UI Contrast for Text Over Background Images
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Enhance text readability by adding configurable overlays or text shadows to improve contrast against various background images.

### Details

Background images can reduce text visibility. This feature will allow users to configure:

- Semi-transparent overlays behind text
- Text shadows for titles and timer digits

Environment variables (optional):

- `TEXT_OVERLAY_OPACITY` — numeric value (e.g., 0.0 to 1.0) controlling overlay transparency
- `TEXT_SHADOW_ENABLED` — boolean to toggle text shadows

Settings should be customizable per page if multiple pages are supported.

### Related Issues

_No response_

### Priority

Medium

### Additional Notes

- Ensure overlays do not obscure important background details if possible.
- Test across different image types and screen sizes.

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Custom Favicon Support with File or URL Option
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Allow users to customize the favicon displayed in the browser tab by providing either a URL or uploading a local favicon file.

### Details

Currently, favicon customization is limited or non-existent. This feature should enable:

- Setting a favicon via environment variable URL
- Uploading a local favicon file, especially useful for self-hosting

In multi-page support, allow different favicons per page.

Environment variables (optional):

- `FAVICON_URL` — URL string pointing to favicon image
- `FAVICON_FILE_PATH` — path to favicon file mounted via Docker volume or accessible by the app

### Related Issues

_No response_

### Priority

Medium

### Additional Notes

- Favicon file support requires handling file uploads or volume mounts.
- Validate favicon format and size for browser compatibility.

sub_issues.title: [Feature] Implement Multi-Page Countdown Support with Per-Page Customizations
sub_issues.author: yiddytlq
sub_issues.body:
### Summary

Enable the application to support multiple countdown pages, each with independent customization options.

### Details

Users can define multiple countdown pages through environment variables or a JSON/YAML config file.

Each page should support:

- Unique countdown targets and titles
- Individual UI customization (colors, fonts, overlays, favicon, etc.)
- Custom favicon per page
- Configurable URLs (e.g., `/page1`, `/page2`)
- Default page redirection from root URL

Admin page (optional) to manage pages dynamically should sync with config files.

Environment variables:

- `DEFAULT_PAGE` — the page shown when visiting root URL
- `PAGES_CONFIG_PATH` — path to JSON/YAML config file with page definitions

Ensure smooth routing and navigation between pages.

### Related Issues

_No response_

### Priority

Medium

### Additional Notes

- Consider caching or in-memory storage for config for performance.
- Admin changes should reflect immediately if possible.

Responsive support for different screen sizes is optional but recommended.

When multiple countdown pages are supported, each page should be able to have independent font size settings.

Environment variable (optional): `TIMER_FONT_SIZE` — CSS font-size value for countdown digits (e.g., `2rem`, `24px`).

- Validate input to avoid broken styles.
